description: Sabotages of win-etw-sys that only a trace session can catch: tests/session.rs, run with --include-ignored. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1 from an elevated process or one in the Performance Log Users group, as CI's runners are (WE-D-3); unelevated, every session test fails to start and the baseline is red, so the sweep stops before any entry.
notCoveredHere: What a unit test can see is sabotage.json.

sabotages.name: WE-D-4: the activity given is not passed to the call
sabotages.why: The activity id the caller gives is what lets a begin and its end written on two threads be one activity; passed as null, the call takes each thread's own.

sabotages.name: WE-D-4: the activity and the related activity are passed in each other's places
sabotages.why: The call takes the activity before the related one; swapped, a start event is recorded as the activity it was related to.
find: unsafe { EventWriteTransfer(self.handle, &raw, activity, related, count, blocks) };
replace: unsafe { EventWriteTransfer(self.handle, &raw, related, activity, count, blocks) };

sabotages.name: WE-D-4: the related activity given is not passed to the call
sabotages.why: A related id the caller gave and the call never saw is a parent the trace does not record.

sabotages.name: WE-D-4: a session reads no related activity
sabotages.why: The reader is how the tests see what the call wrote; one that drops the related id would let the call drop it unseen.

sabotages.name: WE-D-4: a session takes another extended item for the related activity
sabotages.why: The related id is the item of its own type, and no other item is read as one.

sabotages.name: WE-D-4 control: no related activity is passed by another spelling of null
sabotages.why: A control: the same null by another spelling, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.
